Kid, the Jedi temple isn't a place for games. Now, run along.|translated=1|TT-8L-OT speaking in binary|audio=TT-8L-OT-Binary-RevengeJustice.flac|{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}}}} '''TT-8L-OT''' was a surly [[TT-8L gatekeeper droid]] employed by the [[Jedi Order]] to screen those who wished to enter the entrance to the [[Olega Jedi temple|Jedi temple]] on the [[planet]] [[Olega]] outside of its open [[Standard hour|hours]]. In [[132 BBY]], the street urchin [[Guthan Archi]] drew the [[droid]] out of the wall by throwing a rock and then drew TT-8L-OT's attention until the [[Sith assassin|assassin]] [[Mae-ho Aniseya]] forced the gatekeeper to power down by throwing a [[magnet]]ic [[restraining bolt]] at it. Aniseya then [[Skirmish on Olega|entered]] the [[Jedi temple|temple]] to [[Mae's quest|assassinate]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Torbin]] but was forced to flee before she succeeded. ==Biography== ===Distracted doorkeeper=== {{Quote|Hello! I'm over here, come on!''"
«''This is your final warning!''»|quoteend=0|Guthan Archi distracts TT-8L-OT|audio=Urchin-TT-8L-OT-RevengeJustice.flac|}} [[FIle:UrchinRockThrow-RevengeJustice.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=Guthan Archi hurls a rock at TT-8L-OT's head shield while the droid is retracted inside the Olega Jedi temple wall beside a shielded doorway.|Guthan Archi threw a rock at TT-8L-OT and distracted it.]] TT-8L-OT was a [[TT-8L gatekeeper droid]] that the [[Jedi Order]] employed during the [[High Republic Era]]. Stationed in the wall by the entryway of the [[Olega Jedi temple|Jedi temple]] on the [[planet]] [[Olega]], it was responsible for screening passersby who wished to enter the [[Jedi temple|temple]]'s closed doors outside of the open [[Standard hour|hours]] when visitors could freely petition the [[Jedi]]. In [[132 BBY]],{{TheAcolyteDate}} the [[Sith assassin|assassin]] [[Mae-ho Aniseya]] was [[Mae's quest|tasked]] with [[Death|killing]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Torbin]] within the temple and hired a local street urchin named [[Guthan Archi]] to aid her in bypassing TT-8L-OT. [[Thief|Stealing]] a rock{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}} {{AD|Disney+}} from the cart of the passing [[Junk dealer|scrap merchant]] [[Anbert Dregil]] at dusk, Archi hurled it at the [[Security droid|gatekeeper droid]]'s head covering on the temple's wall, causing TT-8L-OT to pop its head out and blink its [[photoreceptor]]s. [[Language|Speaking]] in [[binary]], it questioned who had thrown the rock before spotting the [[Youngling|young]] urchin and warning him that the temple was no place for games. Archi ignored TT-8L-OT's instruction to leave and waved his arms at the [[droid]], calling out to it to draw the gatekeeper's attention. ===Powered down=== {{Quote|Did you activate the security droid? Hmm?''"
[The urchin nods]
"''Why did you activate it?''"
"''She paid me to.|Jecki Lon interrogates Guthan Archi|audio=Jecki-Urchin-RevengeJustice.flac|}} [[File:TT-8L-OT-Restrained-RevengeJustice.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=TT-8L-OT retracts back into the Olega Jedi temple wall with a flashing red restrining bolt attatched to its head.|TT-8L-OT was powered down by Mae-ho Aniseya's restraining bolt.]] Focused on the urchin as it issued a final warning, TT-8L-OT did not see Aniseya emerge from a nearby alcove and hurl a [[magnet]]ic [[restraining bolt]], which attached to the top of TT-8L-OT's head. Frantically beeping, the droid's head juddered from side to side and then powered down before retracting into the wall. Aniseya then paid the urchin for the distraction and [[Skirmish on Olega|entered]] the temple unimpeded but was forced to flee before she could kill Torbin when her break-in was discovered. When investigating the break-in, the temple's Jedi learned that TT-8L-OT had spotted Archi before it failed, resulting in the capture and interrogation of Aniseya's accomplice. [[Od Keder]], one of the temple's [[Padawan]]s, then mentioned the failure of the temple's gatekeeper droids when presenting the urchin to a group of Jedi led by Jedi Master [[Sol]], who had arrived from offworld to investigate. Sol's Padawan, [[Jecki Lon]], then questioned the urchin about why he had activated the droid, learning that Aniseya had paid the child. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|But before the gatekeeper droids failed, they caught this little scoundrel, messing around our portcullis.|Od Keder mentions TT-8L-OT|audio=OlegaPadawan-Scoundrel-RevengeJustice.flac|}} TT-8L-OT monitored the temple doors tirelessly, but a misloaded program updated gave the droid a surly personality. Unlike similar models of droid, it had binocular vision due to its two spheroid, [[Color|yellow]] photoreceptors on extendable eyestalks which it used to scrutinize the world around it. TT-8L-OT was also equipped with a protective shield above its head that signaled approaching visitors. The droid's plating was brown, and it spoke in binary. ==Behind the scenes== ===Design=== {{Quote|We didn't want to copy ''Return of the Jedi'', because it's been done before. But if we're on version twenty by then, this was version one. He had this hat that was the closing mechanism.|Kevin Jenkins|''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]''}} [[File:AndrewMerrison-GatekeeperDroidBlueprints-ArtOfTheAcolyte.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=A set of annotated blueprints showing TT-8L-OT from several angles with measurements for each.|TT-8L-OT was built into a wall of the set with puppeteers behind.]] TT-8L-OT first appeared in "[[Revenge / Justice]]," the second episode of the live-action [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which aired on [[June 4]], [[2024]].{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-teaser-poster|text=''The Acolyte'' Teaser Poster, Premiere Date Revealed}} The droid was first identified by name in its [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry on [[StarWars.com]], which was posted by [[June 5]] of the same year.{{WookCite|url=TT-8L-OT?oldid=13487995|text=June 5, 2024 revision of the "TT-8L-OT" article}} Concept art of the droid titled "Gatekeeper droid" was created by [[Adam Brockbank]] under supervision of production designer [[Kevin Jenkins]].{{Instagram|username=brockbankadam|url=p/C9uBfZgK9_f|author=[[Adam Brockbank]]|date=2024-07-22|quote=Gatekeeper droid The Acolyte Production designer Kevin Jenkins #theacolyte #starwars #starwarsconceptart #conceptart #conceptartist|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/WXqrl|archivefile=File:AdamBrockbank-GatekeeperDroid-Instagram.png}} According to Jenkins, they did not want to copy the [[TT-8L/Y7 gatekeeper droid|gatekeeper droid]] seen in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film{{Film|VI}} [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], as it had been done before, but they considered TT-8L-OT to be a much earlier iteration of that model. Draftsperson [[Andrew Merrison]] created blueprints for the construction of TT-8L-OT that showed the entire length of the prop as five foot three inches, with one foot three inches behind the wall, one foot six inches between the wall and the pivot that the droid's head was mounted on, six inches between the pivot and the front of the droid's photoreceptor, and two inches between the front of the droid's photoreceptor and the edge of the front rim of the disc on its head. The droid's eyeline was five foot seven inches off the ground, with the droid's neck sitting at five foot three inches. A one-foot hole was cut into the wall for the droid to extend through with an eight-inch return behind it and a blacked-out tent set up behind the hole. According to model making supervisor [[Paul Szebesta]], the team worked closely with the construction and art departments to integrate TT-8L-OT into the set in a way they had not done before, with a large framework behind the wall where puppeteers would be able to control the droid without being visible. ===Construction and performance=== {{Quote|We worked closely with construction and the art department to intergrate the droid into the set in a way we've not done before. Performance was important, so we constructed a large framework behind the wall on set, which allowed puppeteers to perform the droid from behind without being seen. T-8L was a bit like an iceberg; what you see pop out on set is only half the picture.|Paul Szebesta|}} [[File:GatekeeperDroid-AdamBrockback-Instagram.jpg|thumb|left|300px|alt=Concept art showing TT-8L-OT emerging from a brown wall.|"Gatekeeper droid," by Adam Brockbank]] Junior animatronic designer [[Matthew Hart]] and{{Instagram|username=theforge_props|url=p/C8aNJZGuGa_|name=[[Mitchell Chamberlain]]|date=2024-06-19|quote=The first proper droid I ever built - and probably the first thing I've made for film/TV that has its own entry in a database! The TT-8L-OT Gatekeeper droid. I worked with @matt.hart87 to build the 3d model around his animatronics, and to have access points in case anything went wrong. There was some model making and some 3d printing - getting the eyes to look right and function properly took some working out (but we got there in the end!) I did a little bit of the base coating, but I believe @paulszebesta did most of the painting and weathering on this one, and @samijohnson123 built his little hat/wall plug. @ashflash_26 built everything past the wall (the rail system for him to slide in and out seamlessly, and look up and down) The amazing @claireroiharvey, @mikequinnstudios, and I think it was Colin (can't find his Instagram!) were responsible for most of his puppeteering - I even got to play around with him a bit one cold Saturday for some of the less important shots! It was always a dream I thought would never come true to build droids for Star Wars - and I'm going to be saying this a lot over the coming months, but I'm always so grateful (and sometimes in utter disbelief) that I got the opportunity.|archivefile=File:TT-8L-OT-Instagram.png}} modeler [[Mitchell Chamberlain]] worked together to build the model around the droid's animatronic using model making and 3D printing, leaving access points to the mechanism in case anything went wrong. According to Chamberlain, the eyes were especially difficult to get right. Chamberlain applied some of the base coating to the model and believes that modelmaking supervisor Szebesta then completed the rest of the painting and weathering. Modeler [[Samuel Johnson]] created the disc on top of the model's head and the wall mount and animatronic designer [[Ashton McCarthy-Gould]] built the parts of the character's mechanism behind the set's wall, including the rail system it slid out of the wall on and the ability for TT-8L-OT's head to move up and down. Droid puppeteers [[Claire Roi Harvey]], [[Colin Purves]], and [[Mike Quinn]] did most of the puppeteering for the droid, with Quinn controlling the droid's entrance and exit from the wall and the movements of its head during close-ups.{{Facebook|username=MikeQuinnOfficial|url=photo/?fbid=997027082432427&set=a.120417703426707|name=[[Mike Quinn]]|date=2024-06-09|quote=👽 Other creatures from the first two episodes I performed on were non-speaking roles. Selkath’s face (eyes & mouth) in the Jedi Temple, costume performed by Liam Cook. The cart puller (face), costume performed by Nick Kellington, who exhibited superhuman strength 🤣. The third was TT-8L-0T the entry droid, performing the entrance, exit and head up/down on the closeups. All super fun and amazing builds from the entire CFX team. This stuff looks so good and is capable of much more scrutiny that is seen on screen. It’s that good! Even for the background creatures. Well done every single person involved! Also a shoutout to the amazing crew who supported and championed us, helped us look beautiful on camera (and encouraged me to say naughty things with my animatronics 😉).|archivedate=2024-06-24|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/7ecW5}} Chamberlain also did some puppeteering work for less important shots. The Olega street scenes including TT-8L-OT were shot on the backlot at [[Shinfield Studios]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]]. ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} {{Mediacat|soundcat=|Audio files of TT-8L-OT|imagecat=Images of TT-8L-OT}} *{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}} {{1st}} ==Sources== *''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' *''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' *{{Databank|tt-8l-ot|TT-8L-OT}} {{1stID|TT-8L-OT}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |es=TT-8L-OT |fr=TT-8L-OT |ka=TT-8L-OT |nl=TT-8L-OT }} [[Category:Droids of the Jedi Order]] [[Category:Droids with it/its pronouns]] [[Category:Droids with unspecified gender programming]] [[Category:Gatekeeper droids]]
